title: SkewGuard-PoLR: Investigating Dirichlet-Uncertainty Gated Multi-Cluster Expansion for Prefix-Consensus Self-Consistency

contributions.purpose: Hedge against incorrect dominant-cluster selection in prefix-consensus self-consistency (PoLR).
contributions.mechanism: Propose SkewGuard-PoLR, placing a Dirichlet posterior over cluster proportions and triggering multi-cluster expansion when the credible set indicates uncertainty about cluster dominance.
contributions.evaluation: Presented as a principled Bayesian extension of PoLR that expands all clusters within a credible set when dominance is ambiguous.
contributions.domain: Test-time scaling / self-consistency for LLM reasoning
contributions.source_quote: we propose SkewGuard-PoLR, a method that uses Dirichlet posterior uncertainty to expand multiple prefix clusters when dominance is ambiguous, providing a principled approach to hedge against incorrect cluster selection.

contributions.purpose: Test whether PoLR's reported tail failures reproduce.
contributions.mechanism: Re-run PoLR on AIME25 with QwQ-32B and compare accuracy against self-consistency (SC).
contributions.evaluation: PoLR achieves 78.89% on AIME25, outperforming SC (77.78%) by +1.11 percentage points rather than the previously reported -10 point degradation; tail failures do not reproduce.
contributions.source_quote: we demonstrate that PoLR's reported tail failures on AIME25 do not reproduce in our evaluation, with PoLR achieving +1.11 percentage points over self-consistency rather than the reported -10 percentage point degradation.

contributions.purpose: Establish the generality of the non-reproduction result and the redundancy of the proposed extension.
contributions.mechanism: Run comprehensive experiments across two models (QwQ-32B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B) and two benchmarks (AIME25, GPQA-Diamond).
contributions.evaluation: SkewGuard-PoLR yields no accuracy improvement while incurring 17-32% higher computational cost, showing uncertainty-based multi-cluster expansion is unnecessary when PoLR's tail failures do not manifest.
contributions.source_quote: we provide comprehensive experiments across two models (QwQ-32B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B) and two benchmarks (AIME25, GPQA-Diamond), showing that uncertainty-based multi-cluster expansion is unnecessary when PoLR's tail failures do not manifest.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Path of Least Resistance (PoLR) (Jindal et al. 2026) addresses this efficiency challenge by exploiting prefix consistency ... We hypothesize that such tail failures occur when cluster dominance is statistically unreliable ... To address this, we propose SkewGuard-PoLR, which uses Bayesian uncertainty quantification to decide when to expand beyond the dominant cluster.

Our work extends PoLR with Dirichlet-based uncertainty quantification over cluster dominance, aiming to expand multiple clusters when the dominant cluster is uncertain. However, our experiments reveal that the prerequisite condition—PoLR exhibiting tail failures when the dominant cluster is incorrect—does not reproduce in our evaluation, rendering the proposed extension unnecessary.

notes: Explicit negative result plus a baseline reproduction failure: the motivating premise (PoLR's reported -10pp tail failure on AIME25 from Jindal et al. 2026) fails to reproduce (PoLR is +1.11pp over SC), so the proposed SkewGuard-PoLR gives no accuracy gain while adding 17-32% compute cost.
